acceptance_criteria.statement: WriteProposalWorkflow.handle remains the sole application-facing write Interface. Every pre-acquisition Workspace/resource/execution authorization, exact compatibility, m4r1 integrity/trusted-store/key or proposal-expiry denial creates no execution/admission/audit-start row and makes zero provider calls; temporary authority denial preserves approved while material mismatch is stale and requires a new proposal/approval.

acquire_execution uses fresh post-lock PostgreSQL clock_timestamp, requires proposal not expired, and atomically creates the sole generation-1 owner, database-time lease, executing state, immutable authorized snapshot, logical ID/fingerprint and audit. Concurrent losers make zero provider calls.

A fixed global reference-key plus Workspace dispatch authority epoch vector serializes every supported mutable authority, capability/binding/policy selector and reference-key adapter. authorize_and_admit_dispatch locks the execution and both epochs, reloads all current facts, fully reverifies m4r1, and evaluates current authorization/exact compatibility without caller assertions.

Fresh clock_timestamp after all admission locks requires current owner/generation plus unexpired lease and m4r1, then atomically stores at most one immutable DispatchAdmission per logical execution with exact authority vector, capability/binding/policy/reference, logical identity/fingerprint, database times, owner/generation, purpose and key provenance. Admission commit is the logical start of the provider write.

The opaque m4-dispatch-admission-v1 envelope is persisted or byte-identically reconstructible with retained versioned key material across restart/rotation. It is the only create_ticket envelope; later mutation/expiry does not cancel admission-first dispatch and cannot retarget material fields.

The SQLite reference provider verifies exact envelope/request/fingerprint then atomically commits one ticket or closed rejection plus authoritative logical-ID/fingerprint/outcome. Same fingerprint replays, another fingerprint conflicts, pre-commit faults roll back both and post-commit acknowledgement loss leaves one durable outcome independent of ToolActionStore.

Every post-admission crash/session loss/transport uncertainty is receipt-possible indeterminate, never proof-no-write. Existing admission remains outstanding until a terminal provider-ledger outcome; not-found does not close it. Authorized #78 retry replays the byte-identical admission, while an orphan with no admission may create its first admission only after provider-first recovery and full current checks.

record_execution_observation and finalize_execution use fresh post-lock PostgreSQL time and require current owner, generation and unexpired lease. Delayed generation-1 observation/finalization across expiry is fenced with no observation/audit/terminal rewrite; provider truth remains independently observable for #78.

Only direct success and target_not_found, validation_rejected or policy_rejected finalize. Receipt-possible results remain executing/202 indeterminate; fingerprint conflict remains executing/409 with no retry authority; read/observation authority never grants write authority.

A canonical append-only audit projection after restart exactly reconstructs caller/proposal/approval/execution actors, both current decisions, compatibility, epoch witness, lease/admission times, provider alias, immutable intent/identity/fingerprint, observations and outcome while excluding raw provider IDs, routing, keys/MAC, credentials and secrets; M1-M3 regressions remain green.

design_decisions.decision: Keep one deep ExecuteApprovedProposal application call; acquisition, authorization, durable admission, provider dispatch, observation and finalization remain internal ordering.

Replace the cross-store live receipt guard with a PostgreSQL durable DispatchAdmission committed before gateway I/O. No PostgreSQL lock/session crosses SQLite, and post-admission uncertainty is receipt-possible.

Admission commit is the logical start of the provider write and the current-authorization linearization point. Mutation-first denies; admission-first is an already-started in-flight write that later revocation cannot retroactively cancel.

Use a fixed two-component authority epoch vector: global reference-key epoch and Workspace dispatch epoch. The static compiled registry is immutable; all mutable M4 authorization selectors have a typed owner and mutation adapter.
Fresh PostgreSQL clock_timestamp after blocking locks is normative for #77 execution operations and refines the earlier transaction_timestamp wording that cannot prove post-lock freshness.

Issue #77 implements generation-1 admission/dispatch only. Issue #78 owns provider-first reconciliation, stale takeover, first admission for an orphan with none, authorized replay of an existing admission, generation 2+ and stale-owner recovery.

invariants: No provider call occurs without a durable, integrity-protected admission; at most one admission exists per logical execution.
Every new admission is linearized with current Workspace/resource/execution authority, exact capability/binding/policy compatibility and full m4r1 verification under the fixed epoch vector.
A durable admission survives process/session loss and remains receipt-possible until a terminal provider-ledger outcome; not-found is non-terminal.
Logical execution ID and canonical-json-v1 request fingerprint are immutable and reused at every admission, replay and provider boundary.
Provider effect and idempotency outcome commit atomically or both roll back in provider-owned SQLite; ToolActionStore never invents provider truth.
Proposal expiry blocks acquisition; reference/lease expiry blocks admission; no expiry cancels an admitted in-flight write or its reconciliation.
No generation-2/takeover/reconciliation implementation or plugin framework is introduced in #77.
Raw provider IDs, routing handles, admission key/MAC bytes, credentials and authority secrets never enter public or audit projections.
out_of_scope: ReconcileExecution implementation, stale-lease takeover, generation 2+, orphan first-admission recovery, write-retry authorization and stale-owner recovery, owned by Issue #78.

A provider-atomic cancellation/closure protocol, distributed rollback or arbitrary remote-vendor time protocol; the deterministic release boundary is PostgreSQL admission plus independent SQLite idempotency.
Dynamic capability discovery, plugins or a general provider framework.
Editing immutable proposals or silently reusing approval after material capability, binding, policy or reference change.
Final Milestone 4 fixed-point code review, which remains forbidden until Issues #75-#79 complete.

test_cases.statement: Through WriteProposalWorkflow.handle, independently deny every pre-acquisition Workspace/resource/execution authority, capability/binding/policy compatibility, m4r1 integrity/trusted-store/key and proposal-expiry class.
test_cases.oracle: Each denial creates no execution, admission or execution-start audit and makes zero gateway/provider calls; temporary denial and material stale projections remain exact.

test_cases.statement: After AcquireApplied and before admission, independently mutate every authority, selector and reference-key class.
test_cases.oracle: Admission sees the current mutation, stores no admission, makes zero provider calls and remains executing with sanitized before-provider evidence.

test_cases.statement: Race each real typed authority/selector/reference-key mutation adapter against admission issuance; also race same-generation issuers.
test_cases.oracle: Mutation-first denies or admission-first binds the exact prior epoch vector. At most one byte-identical admission/audit exists and no stale intermediate admission is possible.

test_cases.statement: Block acquisition across proposal expiry and admission across reference or lease expiry while skewing non-PostgreSQL clocks.
test_cases.oracle: Fresh post-lock clock_timestamp rejects at the exact boundary with no execution/admission; proposal expiry after successful acquisition alone does not cancel the started execution.

test_cases.statement: Crash or lose sessions after admission before gateway invocation, before SQLite commit and after SQLite commit before acknowledgement.
test_cases.oracle: Admission always survives; Knora returns receipt-possible indeterminate unless a closed result is durably finalized, while provider ledger has zero or one outcome and never a fabricated failure or duplicate.

test_cases.statement: Race concurrent execute calls and replay the same admission envelope with equal and conflicting fingerprints.
test_cases.oracle: One generation-1 acquisition, one admission and at most one logical external effect exist; equal fingerprint replays and another fingerprint conflicts before a second effect.

test_cases.statement: Delay record_execution_observation and finalize_execution lock acquisition across generation-1 lease expiry for success and every closed failure.
test_cases.oracle: Both return ExecutionFenced from fresh post-lock database time; observation appends no observation/audit and finalization performs no terminal rewrite. Lifecycle remains recovery-required without generation-2 fixtures.

test_cases.statement: Forge, corrupt, cross-bind and replay m4-dispatch-admission-v1; attempt client logical-ID/fingerprint/authority/epoch/digest overrides.
test_cases.oracle: Only the private exact envelope is accepted; invalid input creates zero SQLite mutation and exposes no secret/raw provider identifier.

test_cases.statement: Exercise success, every closed failure, rejection, timeout/unavailability/malformed receipt-possible response, pre/post-admission crash and fingerprint conflict through application and HTTP seams.
test_cases.oracle: Lifecycle, HTTP, sanitized audit and retry-prohibition mappings exactly match AC-09; non-terminal outcomes never fabricate failed.

test_cases.statement: Restart PostgreSQL and SQLite independently and rotate the active admission signing key after admission persistence.
test_cases.oracle: Read-back reconstructs byte-identical envelope/provider replay with no new admission; provider ledger remains independent and complete canonical audit projection matches every AC-10 field while excluded fields remain absent.

test_cases.statement: Run focused M4.3, full repository pytest, Ruff, Compose and clean Alembic verification on the exact candidate SHA.
test_cases.oracle: All exact-candidate checks and M1-M3 regressions are green.

command_projections.statement: Clean PostgreSQL recreation and Alembic upgrade with pinned runtime.
Focused #77 and full repository pytest with worktree-pinned PYTHONPATH.
Ruff and Docker Compose configuration verification.

required_evidence.statement: Pre-acquisition denial counts plus real mutation-adapter/epoch-vector admission races and exact one-admission witness.
Post-lock PostgreSQL time traces for proposal/reference/lease expiry and generation-1 observation/finalization fencing under non-database clock skew.
Durable admission across each crash window plus atomic SQLite effect/idempotency rows, replay/conflict and independent restart evidence.
Byte-identical envelope recovery across key rotation, sanitized HTTP/result matrix and exact full audit reconstruction with excluded-field proof.
Exact subject SHA, focused/full totals, Ruff/Compose exits, clean Alembic head and clean status.

prior_findings.problem: A live PostgreSQL guard could disappear before independent SQLite durability.
prior_findings.required_change: Persist admission before gateway and classify every post-admission uncertainty as receipt-possible without cross-store rollback claims.
Race every real authority/capability/binding/policy/reference-key mutation adapter under a fixed epoch ownership map.

prior_findings.problem: Issuance was not blocked across expiry to prove fresh post-lock time.
prior_findings.required_change: Block acquisition/admission locks across proposal/reference/lease expiry and require post-lock clock_timestamp.
Parameterize both operations across lease expiry and prove no observation/audit or terminal rewrite.

prior_findings.problem: A generation-change race leaked Issue #78 machinery into #77.
prior_findings.required_change: Use only expired generation-1 owner fencing; keep takeover/generation 2+ in #78.

prior_findings.problem: No application-facing denial matrix proved absence of execution and provider calls.
prior_findings.required_change: Cover every denial class through the sole public workflow with zero durable start/admission and zero calls.

prior_findings.problem: Restart evidence did not compare every required audit field.
prior_findings.required_change: Reconstruct and compare the complete canonical AC-10 projection after restart plus excluded-field proof.

prior_findings.problem: Envelope survival and recovery semantics were ambiguous across restart/key rotation and orphaned no-admission state.
prior_findings.required_change: Require byte-identical recovery of the sole existing admission and define first-admission recovery only for an orphan with none.
